items.title: Bill Kirchner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2021
items.q: I mean somebody, there are some great players like for example Chet Baker knew nothing about harmony in a theoretical sense but he had great ears.

ctx.x: For me it begs the question, sometimes you read comments about jazz and I think they’re usually written, not the musician writers, the non-musician writers, who say jazz musicians play what they feel. And I’ve had this debate with myself about how much emotion is connected to improvisation. Is it driven by emotion and feeling or is it driven by more theoretical knowledge? I know what chord I’m playing here and I know that this will sound out, this will sound in. I’m not sure that’s a question but it’s — I’ll let…

Yeah I probably, my answer would be it’s all of the above. I mean certainly emotion should have an important bearing on it because if it isn’t then why are we doing it? But also I mean you have to have a solid either theoretical knowledge or some kind of instinctual thing about the music. I mean somebody, there are some great players like for example Chet Baker knew nothing about harmony in a theoretical sense but he had great ears. So you know I mean he had his own kind of knowledge. You know it was an…
In the years, let’s say the early 70s, I think you had returned to New York.
